historic_survey.survey: Early Settlement Era Styles Historic Context Statement (2025)
historic_survey.note: A Tanforan Cottage, San Francisco Landmark No. 67 — one of the two best-known Greek Revival residences in the city. Altered, but still showing the style in its flattened window crowns, substantial window frames, squared porch columns, Chippendale balustrades, keystone pediment and low-pitch roof.

historical_record.description: Listed in the Junior League of San Francisco's Here Today survey of 1968. One of the Tanforan Cottages, San Francisco City Landmark No. 67, and among the oldest residences in the city; it stood on the edge the 1906 fire reached and stopped at.

Listed as Tanforan Cottage #1 among the properties in the survey area listed in or formally determined eligible for the National Register and the California Register. With the Mission Dolores chapel and cemetery, the statement gives the Tanforan Cottages of the 1850s as the oldest buildings in the neighbourhood to survive the 1906 earthquake and fire.

unknowns: The city's statement on early settlement era styles dates the cottage to about 1854 in its landmark list and to somewhere between 1853 and 1866 in its property type description; the assessor's roll gives 1849.
